page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by eighth-generation custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), this configuration provides direct access to physical hardware without hypervisor virtualization. The server delivers 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz, matching the virtual CPU count with a single execution thread per core. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core suited for scalable enterprise software stacks.

Hardware resource allocation is characterized by compute density and dedicated throughput. The instance includes 400 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large distributed data transfers and synchronized node communication. There are no onboard local storage volumes, requiring reliance on external block storage configurations, nor are there discrete GPU accelerators attached. This resource balance focuses entirely on raw, unvirtualized ARM compute capacity and substantial memory allocation.

From an architectural standpoint, the dedicated physical core model removes noisy-neighbor effects and context-switching overhead typical of virtualized multi-tenant environments. The uniform 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides predictable resource scaling for multi-threaded systems. Bare-metal access also yields operational cost efficiencies for high-volume workloads by maximizing thread throughput without virtualization penalties, provided the software stack supports native ARM instruction sets.

Amazon Web Services m8gb.metal-48xl is suited for high-density container orchestration, multi-threaded application servers, relational database engines, large CI/CD build farms, and wide-scale microservice deployments that benefit from high core concurrency and high-speed network interfaces.
